spec.description: The job runs python3 examples/tools/build.py 286 --task preservation, the target route of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md (Phase 5 step 1: each deep packet's claim tasks attempted once through the merged path). Example 286 is CVE-2022-22968 (Spring Framework 5.3.18 -> 5.3.19, case-sensitive disallowed-field patterns in DataBinder), prepared by the published-artifact route (pinned Central JARs). Workflow plans the task from target.json; runtime prepares vulnerable-release and fixed-release, runs the packet's controls in separate JVMs on JDK 21 and 25, then runs jvmcontract prove (built by the runner from lib/ at this commit) with --engine native --gaps strict on org.springframework.validation.DataBinder#isAllowed(Ljava/lang/String;)Z with claims/permitted-fields-preserved.json (claim key 93e54e75b16748cd, preservation, bounds unwind 16, maxArrayLength 8). The claim: Outside the allowed change (target.json's preservation task: a field some disallowed pattern matches ignoring ASCII case and none matches exactly), both releases' isAllowed(field), under the same configuration, return the same value or throw the same exception: a field no disallowed pattern matches in any case is allowed exactly when the allowed list is empty or one of its patterns matches it case-sensitively, and a field a disallowed pattern matches exactly is denied, on both. A binder that denies everything satisfies the decision lemma and fails this. Same domain as the decision lemma: ASCII names and patterns, a canonical field, the root locale. Workflow ingests every record into one format-2 receipt under receipts/preservation/, and build.py exits 0 only when the receipt's matchesExpected is true. Its receiver is a DataBinder, which only the packet's adapter builds and the claim has no construction plan for, so a receiver or toLowerCase/Locale refusal is the predicted stop. A capability refusal is a successful diagnostic, not a pass: it gives an unresolved receipt, prints NOT AS EXPECTED and exits 1, and is read as an observed gap for the v1 gap inventory, with the claim left unresolved and never weakened. No proof of this task has been attempted before.
